sentence: The testes, also called the testicles, are a pair of egg-shaped glands that lie in the scrotum, the sac of loose skin below the penis.
note: NCI: two egg-shaped glands (testicles) inside the scrotum, a loose-skin sac directly below the penis; OpenStax calls the same organs testes.

sentence: They make sperm and the hormone testosterone.
note: NCI: testicles produce testosterone and sperm; OpenStax: paired testes make sperm and androgens.

sentence: Sperm pass from each testis into the epididymis, a coiled tube in which they mature, and then along the deferent duct, which joins the duct of the seminal vesicle near the prostate to form the ejaculatory duct.
note: NCI: sperm pass through tubules to the epididymis; SEER/StatPearls: vas deferens meets the seminal vesicle duct near the prostate, forming the ejaculatory duct.

sentence: The seminal vesicles lie behind the bladder and add fluid to the semen.
note: StatPearls: seminal vesicles lie behind the bladder; OpenStax: seminal vesicles contribute the bulk of semen volume.

sentence: A pair of egg-shaped glands inside the scrotum, each a few centimetres long
note: NCI: two egg-shaped glands in the scrotum; OpenStax: paired ovals, each approximately 4 to 5 cm long, here given as a few centimetres.

sentence: Outer tunica vaginalis, then the tough tunica albuginea, which folds inwards to divide the testis into lobules
note: OpenStax: tunica albuginea lies beneath the tunica vaginalis and forms septa dividing the testis into lobules; StatPearls: tunica vaginalis is the outer layer.

sentence: Seminiferous tubules make sperm; Leydig cells between the tubules make testosterone
note: OpenStax: spermatogenesis occurs in seminiferous tubules; key terms: Leydig cells lie between the tubules and produce testosterone.

sentence: Epididymis (head, body and tail), then the deferent duct, which joins the seminal vesicle duct to form the ejaculatory duct
note: SEER: epididymis has head, body and tail; vas deferens joins the seminal vesicle duct to form the ejaculatory duct; StatPearls agrees.

sentence: Kept a few degrees below core body temperature, helped by the dartos and cremaster muscles
note: OpenStax: sperm production is more efficient 2 to 4 degrees C below core temperature; dartos and cremaster raise the testes in cold.

sentence: Testicular arteries from the abdominal aorta just below the renal arteries; veins form the pampiniform plexus
note: StatPearls Testes: testicular arteries arise from the aorta just below the renal arteries; pampiniform plexus drains the testes.

sentence: Ultrasound scan of the testicles and blood tests
note: NHS tests page: tests you may have include blood tests and an ultrasound scan of your testicles.

sentence: Each testis lies in its own compartment of the scrotum, separated from the other testis by the scrotal septum.
note: OpenStax: scrotal septum separates the two testes into compartments; StatPearls: testes lie in the scrotum, separated by the scrotal septum.

sentence: The dartos muscle forms the muscle layer beneath the scrotal skin and continues inwards to form that septum.
note: OpenStax: dartos is the subcutaneous muscle layer of the scrotum and continues internally as the scrotal septum.

sentence: Each testis is covered on the outside by the tunica vaginalis, and beneath this lies the tough, white tunica albuginea.
note: OpenStax: beneath the tunica vaginalis is the tough, white tunica albuginea; StatPearls: tunica vaginalis is the outer layer.

sentence: A spermatic cord supports each testis, and the deferent duct runs through the cord on its way out of the scrotum.
note: MedlinePlus: spermatic cord supports the testes; OpenStax: duct runs through the spermatic cord; StatPearls: duct passes from scrotum to pelvis.

sentence: The two cremaster muscles descend from the internal oblique muscle of the abdominal wall.
note: OpenStax: the two cremaster muscles descend from the internal oblique muscle of the abdominal wall.

sentence: The tunica albuginea also folds inwards to form septa that divide the testis into hundreds of lobules, and the septa converge on the mediastinum testis, which gives the organ structural support.
note: OpenStax: albuginea invaginates to form septa dividing the testis into 300 to 400 lobules; StatPearls: septa converge on the mediastinum testis, its structural support.

sentence: The seminiferous tubules form the bulk of each testis, and sperm are made within them.
note: OpenStax: spermatogenesis occurs in the seminiferous tubules forming the bulk of each testis; SEER: sperm are produced within them.

sentence: The tubules end in straight tubules, the tubuli recti, which pass into the mediastinum and join a network of channels called the rete testis, and efferent ductules then connect the rete testis to the epididymis.
note: Returned summary quoted tubuli recti, rete testis and efferent ductules to epididymis without naming its page; Testes and Endotext were both returned.

sentence: Leydig cells, which lie between the tubules, make testosterone.
note: OpenStax key terms: Leydig cells lie between the seminiferous tubules and produce testosterone; SEER: Leydig cells make testosterone.

sentence: Sertoli cells help control the survival of the developing germ cells, and tight junctions between them form the blood-testis barrier.
note: OpenStax: Sertoli cells are sustentacular cells helping control germ cell survival; tight junctions between them create the blood-testis barrier.

sentence: This barrier keeps bloodborne substances away from the germ cells and stops surface antigens on developing germ cells from escaping into the bloodstream and provoking an autoimmune response.
note: OpenStax: barrier keeps bloodborne substances from germ cells and keeps their surface antigens from escaping and prompting an autoimmune response.

where: section:Epididymis, deferent duct and seminal vesicle
sentence: The epididymis is a coiled tube with a head, a body and a tail.
note: SEER module: epididymis is a coiled tube with three parts, head, body and tail.

where: section:Epididymis, deferent duct and seminal vesicle
sentence: Sperm continue to mature as they pass through it and are stored in the tail until ejaculation.
note: OpenStax: sperm move to the epididymis where they continue to mature; SEER: sperm mature in the body and are stored in the tail.

where: section:Epididymis, deferent duct and seminal vesicle
sentence: The deferent duct is also known as the vas deferens or ductus deferens.
note: Naming equivalence only: the atlas says deferent duct; the returned sources say vas deferens or ductus deferens.

where: section:Epididymis, deferent duct and seminal vesicle
sentence: It continues from the tail of the epididymis, and during ejaculation contraction of smooth muscle pushes sperm from the tail into the duct.
note: OpenStax: smooth muscle contraction pushes sperm from the epididymal tail into the ductus deferens at ejaculation; SEER: vas deferens continues the tail.

where: section:Epididymis, deferent duct and seminal vesicle
sentence: The deferent duct passes from the scrotum through the inguinal canal into the pelvis and then runs behind the prostate, and its far end widens into the ampulla near the back of the bladder.
note: StatPearls: duct runs scrotum, inguinal canal, pelvis, behind prostate; Endotext: dilated distal end forms the ampulla, near the posterior bladder.

where: section:Epididymis, deferent duct and seminal vesicle
sentence: Each seminal vesicle lies behind the bladder and the prostate and above the rectum, beside the ampulla of the deferent duct, and the two join to form the ejaculatory duct, which drains into the prostatic urethra.
note: StatPearls: vesicles lie behind bladder and prostate, above rectum, lateral to an ampulla; the two form the ejaculatory duct, draining to prostatic urethra.

sentence: The testicular arteries arise from the front and side of the abdominal aorta, just below the origin of the renal arteries, with additional supply from the artery of the vas deferens and the cremasteric artery.
note: StatPearls Testes: arteries arise from the anterolateral aorta just below the renal arteries; extra supply from the artery of the vas deferens and cremasteric artery.

sentence: Venous blood leaves through the pampiniform plexus, a network of veins that lies in front of the deferent duct.
note: StatPearls Testes: the pampiniform plexus drains the testes and lies anterior to the vas deferens.

sentence: The testes receive both sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibres.
note: StatPearls Testes: the testes receive both sympathetic and parasympathetic fibres.

sentence: Lymph from the testes follows the same path as the testicular arteries and drains to the preaortic lymph nodes.
note: StatPearls Testes: lymphatic drainage follows the testicular arteries and drains to the preaortic lymph nodes.

sentence: The arteries to the seminal vesicles come from the middle and inferior vesical and middle rectal vessels.
note: StatPearls Seminal Vesicle: arteries come from the middle and inferior vesical and middle rectal vessels.

sentence: The testes make sperm and androgens such as testosterone, and luteinising hormone binds to receptors on the Leydig cells and increases their production of testosterone.
note: OpenStax: testes make sperm and androgens; LH binds Leydig cell receptors and upregulates testosterone production. NCI: testicles produce testosterone and sperm.

sentence: Sperm production proceeds more efficiently when the testes are kept a few degrees below core body temperature.
note: OpenStax: sperm production is more efficient when the testes are 2 to 4 degrees C below core body temperature.

sentence: In cold weather the dartos and cremaster muscles contract to lift the testes towards the body and reduce the surface area of the scrotum, which retains heat; when the temperature rises the scrotum relaxes, which increases its surface area and promotes heat loss.
note: OpenStax: in cold the muscles contract to elevate the testes and decrease scrotal surface area, retaining heat; when warmer the scrotum relaxes, promoting heat loss.

sentence: During ejaculation sperm travel through the deferent duct and mix with fluid from the accessory glands, and the seminal vesicles contribute the bulk of the volume of semen.
note: OpenStax: sperm travel through the ductus deferens at ejaculation and mix with accessory gland fluid; seminal vesicles contribute the bulk of semen volume.

sentence: In testicular torsion the spermatic cord twists, which cuts off the blood supply to the testicle and can cause lasting damage.
note: MedlinePlus: twisting of the spermatic cord, which supports the testes, cuts off blood flow to the testicle and can cause lasting damage.

sentence: The most common sign of torsion is sudden, severe pain in one testicle, and NHS advice is to go straight to A&E or call 999.
note: NHS Essex ICB page: most common sign is sudden, severe pain in one testicle; it advises going straight to A&E or calling 999.

sentence: Epididymo-orchitis is inflammation of the epididymis and the testicle that can be caused by infection.
note: NHS inform: epididymo-orchitis is inflammation of the epididymis and testicle, driven by infections including urine infections, sexually transmitted infections and mumps.

sentence: The NHS says that epididymitis is usually triggered by a sexually transmitted infection or a urine infection, with less common triggers including mumps, tuberculosis and a groin injury.
note: NHS epididymitis page: usually a sexually transmitted infection or urine infection; less common triggers include mumps, tuberculosis and groin injury.

sentence: It causes a tender, warm, swollen scrotum, and some people also have difficulty passing urine or a discharge from the penis.
note: NHS epididymitis page: tender, warm, swollen scrotum; some also have trouble passing urine or a discharge from the penis.

where: section:Clinical relevance: swellings and undescended testes
sentence: Most testicular lumps and swellings are not cancer.
note: NHS inform: most testicular lumps and swellings are non-cancerous; Leeds: the commonest swellings are benign causes.

where: section:Clinical relevance: swellings and undescended testes
sentence: The commonest causes are a hydrocele, a cyst in the epididymis and varicose veins above the testicle, called a varicocele, and these are all benign and need treatment only if they cause significant symptoms.
note: Leeds Teaching Hospitals: usually a hydrocele, epididymal cyst or varicose veins above the testicle (varicocele); all benign, treated only if significant symptoms.

where: section:Clinical relevance: swellings and undescended testes
sentence: A hydrocele is fluid that collects between the layers of the tunica vaginalis, and a varicocele is an abnormal widening of the pampiniform plexus that usually occurs on the left.
note: StatPearls Testes: hydrocele is fluid between the layers of the tunica vaginalis; varicocele is dilatation of the pampiniform plexus, usually left-sided.

where: section:Clinical relevance: swellings and undescended testes
sentence: An undescended testicle has not moved into the scrotum as it usually does, and the condition is common in young children.
note: NHS undescended testicles: a testicle that stays out of its normal scrotal position; a common childhood condition.

where: section:Clinical relevance: swellings and undescended testes
sentence: Often the testicle moves into place on its own, but sometimes surgery is needed, and doctors usually find the problem at the newborn examination.
note: NHS: testicles often move into place on their own, sometimes surgery is needed; usually found at the newborn examination.

where: section:Clinical relevance: swellings and undescended testes
sentence: Left untreated, an undescended testis carries risks of reduced fertility, testicular torsion and a higher risk of testicular cancer.
note: StatPearls summary: untreated undescended testes risk infertility, torsion and testicular cancer; NHS trust text: fertility problems and higher cancer risk.

where: section:Testicular cancer and how it is investigated
sentence: Testicular cancer is a disease in which malignant cells form in the tissue of one or both testicles.
note: NCI: testicular cancer is a disease in which malignant cells form in the tissue of one or both testicles.

where: section:Testicular cancer and how it is investigated
sentence: The NHS lists a lump or swelling in a testicle, a testicle getting bigger, an ache or pain in the testicle or scrotum, and a heavy, firm or hard scrotum as the main symptoms.
note: NHS symptoms page: lump or swelling in a testicle, testicle getting bigger, ache or pain in testicle or scrotum, heavy, firm or hard scrotum.

where: section:Testicular cancer and how it is investigated
sentence: These symptoms can have other causes, but the NHS advises seeing a GP about any of them.
note: NHS symptoms page: see a GP about any of these, but having them does not mean you have cancer.

where: section:Testicular cancer and how it is investigated
sentence: A scrotal ultrasound scan will usually distinguish between benign and cancerous swellings.
note: Leeds Teaching Hospitals: a simple ultrasound scan will usually differentiate between benign and cancerous swellings.

where: section:Testicular cancer and how it is investigated
sentence: When testicular cancer is suspected, the NHS lists blood tests and an ultrasound scan of the testicles among the tests used, after which a specialist explains the results and the next steps.
note: NHS tests page: tests you may have include blood tests and an ultrasound scan of your testicles; a specialist then explains results and next steps.
